sections.Imaging for patients with suspected NSTE: In patients with no recurrence of chest pain, normal ECG and normal levels of cardiac troponin (preferably high sensitivity), but still with suspected ACS, a non-invasive stress test (preferably with imaging) for inducible ischemia or CCTA is recommended before deciding on an invasive approach. In patients with suspected ACS, non-elevated (or uncertain) hs-cTn, no ECG changes and no recurrence of pain, incorporating CCTA or a non-invasive stress imaging test as part of the initial workup should be considered.
sections.Timing of invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS: An early invasive strategy within 24 h is recommended in patients with at least one high-risk criterion (diagnosis of NSTEMI suggested by the diagnostic algorithm; dynamic or presumably new contiguous ST/T-segment changes suggesting ongoing ischemia; transient ST-segment elevation; GRACE risk score >140).
sections.Antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy i: A potent P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor), or clopidogrel if these are not available or contraindicated, is recommended before (or at latest at the time of) PCI and maintained over 12 months, unless contraindicated. Pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in patients undergoing a primary PCI strategy.
sections.Long-term antithrombotic therapy: After stent implantation in patients undergoing a strategy of DAPT, stopping aspirin after 3–6 months should be considered depending on balance between ischemic and bleeding risks. In patients who are event-free after 3–6 months of DAPT and who are not high ischemic risk, SAPT (preferably with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor) should be considered.
sections.Cardiac arrest and out-of-hospital cardi: Delayed as opposed to immediate angiography should be considered among haemodynamically stable patients without ST-segment elevation successfully resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Routine immediate angiography after resuscitated cardiac arrest is not recommended in haemodynamically stable patients without persistent ST-segment elevation.
sections.In-hospital management: When echocardiography is suboptimal/inconclusive, CMR imaging may be considered.
sections.Management of multivessel disease in hae: Routine revascularization of non-IRA lesions should be considered in STEMI patients with multivessel disease before hospital discharge. Complete revascularization is recommended either during the index PCI procedure or within 45 days.
sections.Acute coronary syndrome comorbid conditi: Glucose-lowering therapy should be considered in ACS patients with blood glucose >10 mmol/L (>180 mg/dL), with target adapted to comorbidities; episodes of hypoglycaemia should be avoided. For patients with ACS with persistent hyperglycaemia, glucose-lowering therapy should be considered.
